newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Henderson plans Tokyo listing to boost profile.
newsitem.headline: Henderson plans Tokyo listing to boost profile.

text.p: Henderson Land Development Co Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to become the first Hong Kong company to obtain a secondary listing in Tokyo with a share offer designed to raise its profile and investor base in Japan.

The Hong Kong property developer plans to offer 30 million shares to Japanese investors in the next few weeks. The exact number of shares and issue price have yet to be fixed but the shares are due to list on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on February 5.
"The board considers that the Japan listing and the Japan offering will provide the company with a more diversified investor base," Henderson Land said in a statement.

"The board considers that the Japan listing and Japan offering will further enhance the reputation and familiarity and promote the recognition of the company among banks, financial institutions and investors in Japan and, thereby, increase recognition internationally," the blue-chip company added.

Proceeds of the offering are to be used for general funding purposes and analysts said that while the company had no urgent need for cash, the issue should raise about HK$2 billion (US$258.7 million) based on the HK$72.00 closing price of its shares on Monday.
"That implies that the company is in a net expansion frame of mind," said Franklin Lam, director of research at HG Asia.

Martin Tacon, senior associate at CS First Boston, said most of the big property developers in Hong Kong had large cash requirements due to the expansion of their land banks or large development projects.
"In the back of the company's mind could be future M&A (merger and acquisition) activity or future derivative activity in Tokyo -- in terms of convertible bonds or some other form of bond," he added.
Henderson said it had issued four series of Samurai bonds in Japan in 1995 which were well received by Japanese investors.

While Henderson may not have picked the best time for its listing -- Tokyo shares have plunged recently -- analysts said Japanese investors should find the equity offering attractive since it would give them access to Hong Kong's booming property market and a high-yielding blue-chip stock.
"If you are looking for exposure in Hong Kong you are probably looking for exposure in the property market and this stock is one of the better ones," said one Hong Kong analyst.

Hong Kong's property market is booming, with residential prices continuing to rise this year after gains of some 20-30 percent in 1996. Real estate prices in Japan, on the other hand, have declined since the early 1990s.

"Growth-wise, we are looking for a 30 percent increase in 1997 net profit," the Hong Kong analyst said, adding that the share issue should not dilute Henderson's earnings since it represents only 1.73 percent of the company's enlarged issued share capital.

Lam said the equity offering may point more companies in Tokyo's direction. "If by Henderson's listing it encourages more people in Tokyo to look outside and obviously more at Hong Kong, there will be implications on the costs of funds available for Hong Kong companies in the future," he said.
The offering is subject to approval from the Ministry of Finance in Japan, the Tokyo Stock Exchange and the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong and the completion of certain terms.

Henderson said the shares would be offered at a discount of not more than three percent to the closing price of its shares in Hong Kong at a date closer to the offering. Nomura Securities Co Ltd is due to be lead manager of the offering.
Henderson shares rose HK$0.25 to close at HK$72.25 on Tuesday. They are listed in Hong Kong and also trade in London and, through American Depositary Receipts, in New York. (US$1= HK$7.73)
